::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[How can I insert a subject line in a letter?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/152327/how-can-i-insert-a-subject-line-in-a-letter), asked by [Karlo](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/36500/karlo) on TeX Stack Exchange (2014-01-03; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I am writing a `letter` and I would like to insert a subject line above or below the `\opening`. How should I do this? I prefer not to use `scrlttr2` or `KOMA`.
:::

Here is a modification of the original `letter.cls` that provides a `\subject` command. In a document, `\subject{foo}` will typeset a subject line between the inside address and opening.

## Usage

```latex
\documentclass{letter}
\usepackage{lipsum}% for filler text

\usepackage{etoolbox}
\newcommand{\subjectname}{Subject}
\newcommand{\subject}[1]{\def\thesubject{#1}}
\let\insertsubject\cc
\patchcmd{\insertsubject}{\ccname}{\subjectname}{}{\PatchFailed}
\patchcmd{\opening}{#1}{
    \ifdefined\thesubject%
    \insertsubject{\thesubject}%
    \vspace{\parskip}%
    \fi%
    #1}{}{\PatchFailed}

\signature{Your Name}
\address{Your Address \\ City, State ZIP \\ Country}
\date{\today}

\begin{document}

\begin{letter}{Recipient's Name \\ Recipient's Address \\ City, State ZIP \\ Country}
\subject{Foo bar baz quux}
\opening{Dear [Recipient's Name],}
\lipsum[1-2]
\closing{Sincerely,}
\ps{P.S. Here is a postscript.}
\encl{Enclosures: List here}
\end{letter}

\end{document}
```

## Implementation

The tricky part of implementing this is that the recipient's name and address are declared by the argument of the `letter` environment, but are not typeset until the `\opening` command, before the opening is typeset. So the subject's declaration and typesetting must also be done separately.


* The `\subjectname` command is initialized to `Subject`, but it can be customized with `\renewcommand` to, for example, `Re`.
* The `\subject` command saves its argument in a command `\thesubject`. Each `letter` environment can have its own subject, or the subject can be globally declared in the preamble.
* The command `\insertsubject` is a clone of the `\cc` command (for the carbon copy list used after the letter's signature), but replaces `\ccname` with `\subjectname`. This is to maintain the look and feel of the document. It could be customized to typeset the subject another way.
* Finally, the `\opening` command is patched to insert the subject (if it exists) before the opening.

## Comparison

The other answers abuse the document's schema by adding the subject to either the address or the opening, and furthermore, add presentation elements like font selection and vertical space. I prefer this solution because it maintains the separation of markup and presentation. This is why I decided to exhume this ancient question and add an answer.
